nodes.title: The Map and The Flow
nodes.reading:
Informational friction as a systems problem — why a representation that governs a flow it cannot fully observe tends to deform that flow, under conditions this paper makes explicit. Stated for systems in general, human or not.

Document Status — Foundational Working Paper · Paper 1 · Series: Informational Friction (a systems theory)

The title and section titles are working titles. This is the anchor of the systems-theory series, which re-derives in pure systems terms — independent of whether the agents are human — the object behind three companion series: The Cost of Clarity (information theory), The Attribution Gap (economics), and Human Intelligence Debt (organizational theory). The forward forecasts (the Outlook) and the consolidated falsification battery are deferred to later papers in the series.

nodes.title: Optimization, Coherence, and the Frame
nodes.reading:
Why a system optimizing on its own map cannot see the map; why coherence — not rationality — is the mode that sees it; and why a purely maximizing agent is structurally blind to exactly the capabilities that keep a system alive.

Document Status — Working Paper 2 · Series: Informational Friction (a systems theory)

Builds on Paper 1 ( The Map and the Flow ), which established the object: a representation used as a control surface, diverging from the flow it governs, with back-action. This paper supplies the agent-level mechanism beneath that object. The forward forecasts (the Outlook) and the consolidated falsification battery are deferred to later papers in the series; falsifiable claims are marked inline.

nodes.title: The Outlook
nodes.reading:
What the program forecasts about the near future — anchored on its main prediction: that automation, applied to the systems we actually run, produces more inefficiency and more work before it produces fewer jobs.

Document Status — Companion Paper (The Outlook) · Series: Informational Friction (a systems theory)

This paper gathers the forward forecasts of the whole program — across all four series: The Cost of Clarity (information theory), The Attribution Gap (economics), Human Intelligence Debt (organizational theory), and the systems-theory series (Papers 1–3). Each forecast is conditional: it holds only while the falsification test it rests on survives. Those tests are stated in full in the companion refutation paper; here each forecast names the test it depends on so an examiner can follow the thread.
